question: Can current first-party reciprocity guidance be compiled into an exact typed exposure-time primitive without inventing unreported colour-layer or out-of-range stock behaviour?

kodak_vision3_50d.title: KODAK VISION3 50D Color Negative Film 5203 / 7203 Technical Information

domain_contract.effective_time: positive finite seconds at the same constant incident rate

forbidden: infer colour-layer reciprocity or colour-balance correction from a scalar black-and-white factor
extrapolate Kodak VISION3 50D outside its documented 1/1000-to-1-second interval
treat manufacturer typical guidance as a particular roll, developer, process, temperature or scanner calibration
render photographs or change the AO6/product default from this compiler leaf
fit exponents or change the source table after scoring

branch_rule.pass: retain the typed reciprocity primitive and immediately test the independently stated local-intensity contrast consequence on synthetic exposure fields
branch_rule.fail: repair only a source transcription or numerical defect; do not infer a photographic operator

claim_ceiling: First-party formula compiler and documented identity interval for exposure-time mechanics; not colour-film reciprocity, particular-roll/process calibration, scanner response, photographic quality or product promotion.
